review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

4:1.sourceText: Λαλούντων δὲ αὐτῶν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν, ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς οἱ ἱερεῖς καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι,
4:1.targetText: While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees came up to them,

groups.note: The genitive absolute Λαλούντων αὐτῶν is rendered While … were speaking.

ἐπέστησαν ("stood over, came upon") is rendered came up to.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds guard; the Greek says "the captain of the temple".

4:2.sourceText: διαπονούμενοι διὰ τὸ διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς τὸν λαὸν καὶ καταγγέλλειν ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὴν ἀνάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
4:2.targetText: greatly disturbed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.

groups.note: διὰ τό with the infinitive ("because they were teaching") is rendered that.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The repeated article of the phrase τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐπέβαλον αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ἔθεντο εἰς τήρησιν εἰς τὴν αὔριον· ἦν γὰρ ἑσπέρα ἤδη.

groups.note: ἐπέβαλον … τὰς χεῖρας ("laid their hands on") is rendered seized.

BSB leaves ἤδη ("already") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek verb ἔθεντο has none.

unmappedTarget.reason: N1904 has no article before ἀριθμός; BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

4:31.sourceText: καὶ δεηθέντων αὐτῶν ἐσαλεύθη ὁ τόπος ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν συνηγμένοι, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ἅπαντες τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος, καὶ ἐλάλουν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ μετὰ παρρησίας.
4:31.targetText: After they had prayed, their meeting place was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.

groups.note: The actual praying genitive-absolute clause supplies the antecedent circumstance, rendered After they had prayed; English after expresses that completed-prayer circumstance.

Greek the place in which they were gathered is nominalized as their meeting place. The place noun and its gathering relative clause together supply the contextual possessive nominal phrase; the copula alone does not mean their.

The filling passive takes the Spirit genitive as its content complement; English expresses this verb/complement construction with filled with. The separate Greek Spirit words retain their actual content heads.
The Greek with-boldness manner phrase is expressed by the English adverb boldly; the whole preposition/noun phrase supplies that adverbial meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB omits the opening Greek and at this verse boundary.
